iris.nec.failure.description:
Not Enough Crashes can severely break the game while handling crashes, and does not provide accurate results.
A good alternative is MixinTrace, which can identify the cause of a crash more reliably and does not put the game in an invalid state.

options.iris.shadowDistance.enabled: Allows you to change the maximum distance for shadows. Terrain and entities beyond this distance will not cast shadows. Lowering the shadow distance can significantly increase performance.
options.iris.shadowDistance.disabled: Your current shader pack has already set a render distance for shadows; you cannot change it.
options.iris.shadowDistance.sodium_toolt: The shadow render distance controls how far away terrain can potentially be rendered in the shadow pass. Lower distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates. This option cannot be changed on packs which explicitly specify a shadow render distance. The actual shadow render distance is capped by the View Distance setting.

options.iris.glintBrightness.tooltip: Controls the brightness of Wynncraft glint effects. Lower values dim effects in bright areas, higher values let them shine through.
options.iris.tintBrightness.tooltip: Controls the brightness of Wynncraft armor/weapon tints (color recolors). Adjust if tints appear too bright or too dim.
options.iris.wynncraftSceneDarkening.too: Controls how much the scene fog and lighting is darkened when a Wynncraft dark skybox is active (Stormy, War, Red Lightning). At 100%, full darkening. At 0%, no darkening. Disabled during rain.
options.iris.wynncraftEntityBrightness.t: Controls the brightness boost for non-emissive entities when a Wynncraft dark skybox is active. Emissive entities are excluded because Entity Emissivity controls them separately.
options.iris.wynncraftEntityEmissivity.t: Controls the brightness of Wynncraft emissive entities (rift structures, decorations marked as emissive). At 100%, entities are fully bright. At 0%, normal shader pack lighting applies.
options.iris.wynncraftNightVisionDisable: When enabled, the entity brightness boost from dark skyboxes is disabled while the Night Vision potion effect is active. Turn off if you want the boost to apply regardless of night vision.
options.iris.wynncraftTextBrightnessFloo: Keeps text display entities readable in dark areas by applying a minimum light level without changing their colors.
Sets the minimum light level for text display entities when Text Brightness Floor is enabled. Lower values preserve darker ambience; higher values improve readability.
options.iris.wynncraftMistWoodsFog.toolt: Enables the close fog effect in the Mist Woods area of Fruma, matching the vanilla Wynncraft experience. Disable if you prefer to see further in the Mist Woods.
options.iris.wynncraftMistWoodsFogDensit: Controls how thick the Mist Woods fog is. At 100%, matches vanilla Wynncraft. At 0%, the fog has no visual effect. Only active when Mist Woods Fog is enabled.
options.iris.wynncraftMistWoodsFogMinDis: Sets a minimum distance for the fog to fully engulf. At Default, uses the biome's natural fog distance (about 56 blocks). Higher values push the fog further away while preserving its thickness, letting you see more of the Mist Woods. Only active when Mist Woods Fog is enabled.
options.iris.wynncraftMistWoodsFogSunTin: Reduces the orange/red tint the fog gets when looking toward the sun at sunrise/sunset. Inverts vanilla's directional tint math for a precise result. Use the slider to control the strength.
How strongly to remove the vanilla sun tint from the Mist Woods fog. At 100% the fog uses the biome's pure base color regardless of view direction. Only active when Reduce Sun Tint is enabled.
Attempts to render your equipped armor on Wynncraft's mounted fake-player model. Experimental; disable if armor appears on unrelated player heads.
options.iris.wynncraftAmbienceEnabled.to: Automatically switches shader packs and shader settings from the selected ambience pack based on your location.
options.iris.wynncraftAmbienceAutoWarmCa: Automatically prepares ambience shader presets after an ambience pack is enabled. This avoids first-entry region stutters, but preparing large packs can briefly reduce FPS or pause rendering.
